earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog emok1238 lists only the ISO 639-3 retirement request; extinct, no linguistic description located.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Emok language' (redirects to 'Spurious languages'; section 'Retired 2014': 'Emok [emo] – never existed').
sources.note: Nothing; lists Emok among ISO codes retired because the language never existed.

sources.citation: Glottolog languoid record emok1238 'Emok' (family: Bookkeeping; iso_retirement 2013-012, reason 'non-existent'; Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist).
sources.note: Nothing; bookkeeping entry for a retired, non-existent language; only reference is the ISO change request plus Susnik 1962 'Estudios emok-toba' (description type unknown).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2013. Change Request Number 2013-012: retire [emo] Emok (submitted by Hannes Kalisch, Nengvaanemkeskama Nempayvaam Enlhet; supported by Alain Fabre). Adopted, effective 2014-02-03. SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing; the document establishes that 'an Emok language (classified as extinct) in fact never existed. Emmo'ok is not the name of a language; it means simply "our neighbour" in the languages of the Enlhet-Enenlhet family' (p.2). Code retired as non-existent.

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain. 2005 [internet version, last modified 2021-03-12]. Los pueblos del Gran Chaco y sus lenguas, primera parte: Los enlhet-enenlhet del Chaco Paraguayo. Suplemento Antropológico 40/1: 503-569. 76 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Fn.19 (p.13): Susnik's 'emok-toba' = toba-qom (Guaicuruan) and her bilingualism claim is unsupported; fn.47 (p.71): <emok-liik> arises from a confusion (cp. Toba-Enenlhet /emmoʔok/ 'nuestro pariente, prójimo') and, per Chase Sardi et al. 1990:110, refers to the toba-qom, not the enenlhet-toba.

sources.citation: Susnik, Branislava. 1962. Estudios emok-toba. Asunción (Boletín de la Sociedad Científica del Paraguay / Museo Etnográfico Andrés Barbero series; exact imprint not verified).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: Only work Glottolog attaches to emok1238; would confirm that its linguistic material (if any) is Toba-Qom (toba1269) rather than a distinct language — relevant only for re-keying, not for a stress statement under emok1238.
